title: Architecture documentation
task_statement: Record architecture decisions with their alternatives, owners, evidence, and review criteria so a successor can operate the system. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Architecture decision record
components.first_principle: A record that a successor can read preserves the decision after the original people leave. (Inference)
steps: Write the decision, its date, and its owner. (Inference)
List each alternative and the reason it lost. (Inference)
Record the assumptions and trade-offs of the chosen option. (Inference)
Link the evidence, such as an evaluation run. (Inference)
Write the review criteria that reopen the decision. (Inference)
Record the open issues that remain unresolved. (Inference)
Add a new record that supersedes the old one. Keep the old record unchanged. (Inference)
pros: Lets a successor operate the system without the original team. (Inference)
Keeps the evidence attached to the decision. (Inference)
cons: Records go stale when code changes without a record update. (Inference)
A long record for a small configuration flag adds work with no gain. (Inference)
use_when: A decision is expensive to reverse or affects several components. (Inference)
A new owner will run the system later. (Inference)
do_not_use_when: A configuration flag is easy to revert and has no trade-off. (Inference)
A hackathon demo uses no real data. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Name the current owner of each decision. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Link audit or compliance evidence to the evidence field. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Write the review criteria as measurable thresholds. (Inference)
Write records only for decisions that affect several components. (Inference)
Record the cost per completed task that the decision assumed. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D6.4. Expect a successor scenario with no original owner. The credited answer reads the decision record and checks its review criteria before any change. (Inference)
components.trap: A full new evaluation looks thorough, but it repeats evidence that the record already holds. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Record each decision with its alternatives, owner, evidence, and review criteria when you make it. (Inference)
components.exam_tip: If the decision owner left, the first action reads the record. (Inference)

key_facts.text: A model ID identifies a pinned version that stays constant for the lifetime of that ID.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Anthropic does not update the weights or configuration of a model ID.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Infrastructure updates can change observable behavior even when the model ID and weights stay the same.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Every model ID has its own deprecation and retirement schedule.
key_facts.label: Fact

components.name: Model ID in decision records
components.first_principle: Record the exact model ID, because a dateless ID from the 4.6 generation names one fixed snapshot.
steps: Send the full model ID in each request.
Record the model ID and the platform in the decision record.
Record the deprecation date for that model ID. (Inference)
Test a new model ID before you change the record. (Inference)
Create a new record when the model ID changes. (Inference)
pros: The record matches the exact snapshot that the evaluation measured.
A model upgrade becomes an explicit change to the model ID.
cons: A dateless ID is not an evergreen pointer, because an updated version ships under a new model ID.
Behavior can shift on the same ID after infrastructure updates.
use_when: A decision depends on measured quality or cost for one model.
A platform offers several ID formats for the same model.
do_not_use_when: The decision does not depend on model behavior, such as a storage format choice. (Inference)
The model is a prototype with no decision record. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Record the model ID that the evaluation used. (Inference)
Check the deprecation table before each release.
constraints.combination: Test a successor model well before the retirement date. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Record the platform that hosts the model ID.
constraints.combination: Record the endpoint type, such as global or regional, on Amazon Bedrock. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Record the API version that the client sends.
constraints.combination: Use the latest API version when possible, as the docs recommend.

native_services.text: Model IDs carry an anthropic. prefix, such as anthropic.claude-opus-5-5.

native_services.service: Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed)
native_services.text: Models from the 4.6 generation use the Claude API ID. Earlier models add an at sign and a date.

native_services.service: Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed)
native_services.text: This offering uses the same model IDs as the Claude API.
Model IDs are identical to the Claude API IDs, such as claude-haiku-5-5, with no anthropic. prefix.
The deployment name becomes the model parameter, and it defaults to the model ID.

components.exam_tie: D6.4. Expect a decision record that names a model. The credited answer names the exact model ID and the platform. (Inference)
components.trap: A dateless ID looks like an alias that moves, but it names a fixed snapshot. A record that says latest misstates what was tested.
components.decision_rule: Record the exact model ID, the platform, and the deprecation date for each measured decision.
components.exam_tip: A model ID with no date is a fixed snapshot from the 4.6 generation onward.

key_facts.text: A dateless model ID from the 4.6 generation is a fixed snapshot, not an alias.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Models before the 4.6 generation include a snapshot date in the ID.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Anthropic gives at least 60 days of notice before retirement of a publicly released model.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Microsoft Foundry follows the Claude API lifecycle schedule.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Anthropic recommends the latest API version whenever possible.
key_facts.label: Fact

flowchart LR

  A --> T[Trade-offs]
  T --> E[Evidence link]
  E --> O[Owner]
  O --> R[Review criteria]
  M[Exact model ID] --> E
  R --> S[Supersede, do not edit]
